subject: zoology
question_text: Distinguish between endocrine and exocrine glands with examples.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Endocrine glands
steps.why: A gland with no duct has only one route out for its secretion, and that route is the blood.
common_mistakes: Writing that endocrine glands have fine ducts. They have none, and that is the whole difference.
Calling the secretion an enzyme. Endocrine glands secrete hormones.
steps.memory_tip: Endo means inside: the secretion goes inside, into the blood.
steps.margin_note: Ductless, hormones into blood, two examples. Three short lines.
lines: They pour their secretions, called hormones,

steps.label: Exocrine glands
steps.why: A duct is a tube, so an exocrine secretion can be delivered to one named place, while a hormone with no duct reaches the whole body through the blood.
common_mistakes: Using the same example for both. Salivary glands are exocrine; the thyroid is endocrine.
steps.memory_tip: Exo means outside: the duct carries the secretion outside the gland.
steps.margin_note: The duct is the marked difference. Add two examples on each side.

lines.text: Endocrine: no duct  ·  Exocrine: with duct

lines: Exocrine glands are glands with ducts.
The duct carries the secretion to a surface or
They secrete saliva, mucus, ear wax, oil, milk

insider_note: Write this one as two named halves, not as prose — the examiner ticks 'ductless, hormones, blood' on one side and 'duct' on the other.
